options.text: A molecule that changes the pH
A molecule with a similar shape to the substrate that competes for the active site
A substrate that speeds up the reaction
A molecule that permanently destroys the enzyme

questions.explanation: A competitive inhibitor has a similar shape to the substrate and competes with it for the active site. It blocks the substrate from binding but does not permanently alter the enzyme.

questions.stem: Where does a non-competitive inhibitor bind?

options.text: To an allosteric site away from the active site

questions.explanation: A non-competitive inhibitor binds to an allosteric site on the enzyme, away from the active site. This causes the enzyme to change shape, altering the active site so the substrate can no longer fit.

questions.stem: How can the effect of a competitive inhibitor be overcome?
questions.explanation: Increasing the substrate concentration can overcome competitive inhibition because substrate molecules outcompete the inhibitor for the active site, increasing the chance of successful binding.

questions.stem: Can increasing substrate concentration overcome non-competitive inhibition?

options.text: No, because the inhibitor does not block the active site directly
Only if the inhibitor is removed first
Yes, but only at high temperatures

questions.explanation: Increasing substrate concentration cannot overcome non-competitive inhibition because the inhibitor binds elsewhere on the enzyme and changes the shape of the active site regardless of how much substrate is present.

questions.stem: Which type of inhibitor is used in some medicines like penicillin?
questions.explanation: Penicillin is a competitive inhibitor that blocks the active site of an enzyme needed for bacterial cell wall synthesis, preventing bacteria from building their cell walls.

options.text: When the final product of a metabolic pathway inhibits an enzyme earlier in the pathway
When an enzyme is permanently destroyed

questions.explanation: End-product inhibition (feedback inhibition) is when the final product of a metabolic pathway acts as an inhibitor of an enzyme earlier in the pathway, regulating the rate of production.

questions.stem: A non-competitive inhibitor changes the shape of the:
questions.explanation: When a non-competitive inhibitor binds to an allosteric site on the enzyme, it causes a conformational change that alters the shape of the active site, preventing the substrate from binding.
